text:
devon: quick follow-up from the autoscale sync earlier — i sketched a smaller surface we can ship without the full predictive planner

sara: good. what did you end up putting in the surface?

devon: two primitives: 1) Reserve(headroom_tokens, ttl, priority) - for short bursts / prewarm budgets, 2) Observe(current_qps, p50_lat, p95_lat) - simple telemetry hook. both are intentionally minimal.

miguel: i like Reserve as a first-class op. how do we prevent tenants gaming it (hoarding headroom)?

devon: priority + ttl limits. ops will also enforce accounting at the operator level. Reserve returns a small immutable token id you must present when admitting burst requests. token carries consumed/remaining counters.

sara: are we coupling admission to the operator? i remember concerns about operator owning preemption decisions

devon: operator remains the single source of truth for actual capacity and eviction. admission lives in the pool-proxy and validates tokens with the operator. operator also exposes a thin audit API for token metadata.

chun: curious about operational failure modes: what if operator is partitioned? do we block admissions?

devon: fallback plan: token validation is cached with TTL. if operator unresponsive, proxy can continue to admit based on cached allowance until cache expires, then switch to conservative denial. we should surface these events in the console.

miguel: sounds reasonable. does this change our cost accounting model? we already have per-tenant cost ledgers

devon: it plugs into existing ledger: every Reserve issuance increments a prewarm liability line; consumed tokens convert to chargeable usage. we also maintain burst credits that decay if unused.

sara: i worry about complexity in the operator -> proxy RPCs. can we keep message schemas tiny?

devon: yes. Reserve request: {tenant_id, requested_tokens, ttl, priority}. Reserve response: {token_id, allowed_tokens, expires_at}. Validate: {token_id} -> {allowed_remaining, state}. that's it.

miguel: what about fairness? high-spend tenants shouldn't be able to starve small tenants during bursts

devon: priority + fractional admission. admission policy in proxy will allow small guaranteed slices per tenant (soft reservation) before honoring high-priority bursts. operator provides global headroom budget and a per-tenant ceiling.

chun: testing plan? i want to run a chaos test where operator API is delayed 20s every 5 mins

devon: test matrix: 1) normal load with burst issuance 2) operator partition + cache expiry 3) burst storms from 100 tenants 4) cost accounting reconciliation. collect: token issuance rate, cache miss rate, admission rejects, p50/p95 lat per tenant, billing deltas.

ops-bot: NOTE: created issue infra/eng-runtime#1427 for test harness and chaos script

sara: rollout plan: alpha behind feature flag on dedicated staging pools first. run 2 weeks, verify metrics, then limited prod canary (10% of pools).

miguel: metrics we care about for rollout: tail latency SLO violations, admission reject rate, false-positive evictions, and cost per token. also operator CPU/mem overhead.

chun: edge case: what if multiple proxies try to validate/consume the same token concurrently?
devon: atomic consume handled by operator via an increment/compare loop. proxies do optimistic local decrement and then async reconcile. on conflict operator returns remaining allowance. proxies must reconcile and if over-consumed, apply rollback admission (reject next requests).

sara: can we express this in pseudocode for the operator API and include in RFC?
devon: will add a short appendix to the RFC with message formats and pseudocode. sample below:

```
# Reserve flow (pseudo)
Reserve(req):
  if tenant_quota_exceeded(req.tenant_id): deny
  allowed = min(global_headroom_remaining, req.requested_tokens)
  token = create_token(allowed, expires_at)
  ledger.add_prewarm_liability(req.tenant_id, allowed)
  return token

ValidateConsume(token_id, n):
  atomically:
    if token.remaining >= n:
      token.remaining -= n
      ledger.record_consumption(token.tenant_id, n)
      return {allowed_remaining: token.remaining}
    else:
      return {allowed_remaining: token.remaining, error: 'insufficient'}
```

miguel: nice. small bikeshed: token ids should be opaque and short-lived to avoid telemetry sprawl.

devon: agreed. we'll use 128-bit opaque ids, base62 encoded.

sara: follow-up action items?

devon: I'll: 1) update RFC with API appendix, 2) open PR for proxy validator + cache logic, 3) wire test harness. chun: can you own chaos tests?

chun: yep. will draft chaos scenarios and loadpackets by EOW.

miguel: i'll take the billing reconciliation piece and add asserts to the cost pipeline.

sara: i'll coordinate staging rollout and add SLO dashboards.

oncall-bot: @channel reminder: deploy window tomorrow 0200-0300 UTC. coordinate w/ops if you need blackout

devon: noted. maybe keep Reserve feature flag off for that deploy window.

sara: agreed, we'll schedule the canary later. thanks all :thumbsup:
